images.caption: Figure 1:AnyGameRenderer turns crude gameplay into polished game visuals.Top:one checkpoint handles diverse genres and input types, and renders one input in many styles. Insets show the crude input.Bottom:an agent writes the game and the engine outputs a blockout, which AnyGameRenderer renders into the final visuals. This allows style switching and skips modeling, texturing and animation.

Figure 2:Overview of AnyGameRenderer.(a) Paired data from three sources. GEAR games use multi-stream rendering, which pairs each game render with several aligned crude streams such as blockouts and semantic maps. Unreal Engine scenes use two-stream rendering, which pairs a full render with blockouts. Real gameplay recordings are converted into blockouts by detecting 3D bounding boxes.
(b) One training sample: the crude clip is the input video<Video 1>, the target’s first frame serves as an optional anchor, and a six-segment caption defines which real entity each crude shape represents and what must be preserved.
(c) Text,<Video 1>, anchor, and noisy target tokens form one sequence for the frozen MiniMax-H3 DiT. Only the LoRA adapters on self-attention and feed-forward layers are trained, and the model renders the input gameplay in the prompted style.

Figure 3:Three failures of the zero-shot base model.Red dashed boxes mark the errors.Left:input primitives are left unrendered; the cyan cylinders stay in the output instead of becoming characters.Middle:the input has only two blocks, but the model adds an extra creature that does not exist in the input.Right:the input is a top-down view, but the model renders a frontal group shot.

Figure 4:Zero-shot MiniMax-H3 versus AnyGameRenderer on held-out cases, with the same seed, steps, and caption. The zero-shot model leaves crude shapes unrendered (rows 1–4), drops the input viewpoint for out-of-domain styles (rows 5–6: a top-down blockout becomes a frontal anime scene or a first-person voxel scene), and adds caption-named characters although the input has only two blocks (row 7). AnyGameRenderer fixes all three. For rows 5–6, the “GT” column is the original in-domain render and serves only as a layout reference.

Figure 5:Entity-sync metrics by genre.Zero-shot MiniMax-H3 (orange) versus AnyGameRenderer (blue) on the held-out benchmark, grouped into first-person shooter, top-down, third-person, crowd, and vehicle games.
